221	## Detailed Design
222	
223	### Core Rules
224	
225	Rules are grouped by topic (A-H); ids are stable, not sequential within a group (CT-42 to CT-44 sit with the topic they belong to). Rule ids are `CT-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas); acceptance criteria `AC-CT-n` (Acceptance Criteria) and open questions `OQ-CT-n` (Open Questions). Each rule is stated as **Rule**, **Why**, **Source**. Where two specialist proposals differed and no earlier ruling decided it, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: ...)". Names that Web Map & Transit marks provisional (`web.view`, `web.state`, `transit_state`) are used with that mark carried (WM-36). `HOME_ID` := the `derelict_id` of the `web.view.nodes[]` entry whose `kind` is the home ship (the WM-3 roster `kind`); it is a derived label, never a constant and never registered (WM defines no such constant). Godot-specific mechanisms are not designed here: each is marked "-> ADR candidate" (ADRs (a)-(f) are listed at the end of the section), and anything the engine reference cannot source is marked NOT SOURCEABLE. **Engine reference coverage:** `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/rendering.md`, `VERSION.md` and `breaking-changes.md`; there is **no** `scripting.md` or `core.md`, and nothing on `ConfigFile`, `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode`, `Window` display-mode APIs, `Input.mouse_mode`, key-echo detection, focus-out notifications, font-importer flags or AccessKit property names; those are NOT SOURCEABLE and are routed to the ADRs below.
226	
227	#### A. What the layer is
228	
229	**CT-1. A meta layer, not a place.**
230	*Rule.* The chart table is one PIPE layer-3 `CanvasLayer` in the **root viewport**, opened by the `chart_table` input action (Esc / Start) from the `gameplay` context only (in the pod, on a derelict, in the home-ship). In `inspect_card` the same press is consumed by the Adapter: the card closes first, the context returns to `gameplay`, no event reaches this layer, no `request_pause` is made and no overlay opens, and a running channel is untouched (PC-2 context return table; AC-PCI-170); a second press, now in `gameplay`, opens the layer (TX-13 / TX-14, governed by CT-3). In `chat` (VS-B) the layer does not open *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*. It has no prop, no location, no lighting, no glow, no ambient, no occlusion and no camera jolt. It is scaled by the HUD scale `H` for the bitmap face and continuously for the reading face (PR-12).
231	*Why.* A prop would be a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and could lie; the meta layer is honest by definition (ART 7.0 row 3: "can a reading lie? never"). The chart must be reachable on a sortie, which a home-ship console could not be. An in-world "chart-table console" or ship schematic does not exist (IW-28, C4).
232	*Source.* PIPE:94-103 (PR-3); PC-2 (contexts and context return table); PCI:78; ART 7.0.
233	
234	**CT-2. Truth channel.**
235	*Rule.* Layer 3 is never wrapped by the Perception Filter or by Sanity. No gleam, glide, tremor or settle occurs on any chart, panel or menu element (ART 7.3: the three motion signatures are readings only, and nothing on this layer is a reading). The layer is pixel-identical at sanity stage 0 and at forced stage 3, apart from the world visible beneath the panel. It never carries Violet or Flesh (ART 4.6), and Alarm Red appears on no element, because the layer draws no failing instrument (HR-4: red is never text). The only motion on the layer is the filament drift (CT-13, CT-40), the ART 7.3 cut/fade band and the ART 7.3 bracket ease-out, and the linear hold bar (CT-22).
236	*Why.* P1; ART HR-6 names menu, pause and settings layers as anchors; PF:223 (row 9, TRUTH: the pass sits below every `CanvasLayer`); SN:1226 (TRUTH anchor).
237	*Source.* PIPE PR-3 / PR-10; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-4, HR-6. **Note.** The world frozen or running under the panel keeps whatever it showed, including a lie (CT-4, Player Fantasy "Under hallucination"); the panel does not.
238	
239	**CT-3. Surface architecture: panel first, stable order.**
240	*Rule.* `chart_table` opens the **panel**, a right-third plate over the world (ART 7.4). The panel has exactly four items in this fixed order: **Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit**. The order never changes with state. An item that cannot act is shown **disabled** (the disabled style of CT-VA-7: Hull Grey label and a dashed 1-px Hull Grey border, so it clears the 3:1 glyph floor by shape plus tone; it is no longer Graphite lit, which measured 2.8:1), never hidden *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Default focus on open is Resume (non-destructive). Chart (and any message plate) replaces the panel in a cut (a replacement is not an appearance, so it takes no fade), except under reduce flashing, where it uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band (`CHART_FADE_MS`, CT-13). A replacement that raises layer-3 coverage is a governed raise (the re-open governor below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. "Display & Comfort" opens its page inside the panel's column. The panel carries only item labels and the empty status-line slot that holds `FAILED` when a write fails (CT-17, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); every paragraph of copy lives on a full-bleed **message plate** on the chart-table register (CT-28).
241	*Why.* One entry point; the world stays visible under the panel as ART 7.4 specifies; the HUD (layer 2) stays visible and frozen behind the pause panel, except that an active warning mark is held ON solid (HUD HS-23; the HUD's rule, acknowledged here; the full-bleed chart covers layer 2 entirely); a stable order is a muscle-memory affordance and menu layers are anchors that must not shift (HR-6). The accepted cost is that the chart is two actions from a pause; CT-10 (a no-pick console press opens the chart) offsets it. A second `chart` action stays an Alpha playtest fallback owned by the Player Controller and is not designed here.
242	*Ruled (HR-13, ASK-CT-8, OQ-CT-15, OQ-CT-27): the re-open governor. A player-initiated toggle of a large plate counts toward the 3 Hz ceiling, and the layer and the kernel are rate-limited together, never the picture alone* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director ruling)*.
243	- **Coverage levels.** `c = 0` CLOSED; `c = 1` the panel family (`PANEL`, `SAVE_FAILED`, `DISPLAY_COMFORT` opened from the panel); `c = 2` any full-bleed in-session plate (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`). A **raise** is a transition that increases `c` (TX-13, TX-14, TX-16, TX-17, TX-18, TX-24, TX-25); a **lower** decreases it (TX-15, TX-19, TX-35). Boot-flow screens are not governed (no world is visible under them and they appear once per process).
244	- **Close and resume are never delayed.** Every lower takes effect on the press frame. In SOLO a close calls `request_resume` on that frame.
245	- **A raise that comes less than `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` after the most recent lower is queued** and applied the first presented frame at or after `t_last_lower + CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` on the layer's UI clock (CT-43). A raise with no lower in the preceding interval is applied at once (the first open after a quiet period is never delayed). A queued raise applies **as one unit**: the plate, the focus, and in SOLO the `request_pause` of a CLOSED-to-PANEL or CLOSED-to-CHART raise happen on the same frame, so the picture and the kernel state always match (a queued open leaves the layer CLOSED and the kernel `RUNNING`; it never leaves an opaque plate over a running sim, nor a paused sim with no plate).
246	- **The queue is latched, one slot, and cancellable.** The pressed intent is held even if the key is released before the interval ends; there is one slot (the latest desired raise replaces an earlier queued one); only a `cancel` press while a raise is queued **cancels** it (the layer stays at its current level and a CLOSED layer is never opened and never paused) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: **a repeat `chart_table` press while a raise is queued is idempotent** (the raise stays queued, the latch is unchanged, nothing else happens), because at the first-launch default the lag is 1,000 ms and a player who pauses within a second of resuming (Moment 2, an emergency action) presses Esc twice from impatience and must not end up unpaused. **Queued acknowledgement:** the queue gives an audio-only acknowledgement (a single cue, no visual element, so no flash risk) requested from Adaptive Audio (ASK-CT-20; the layer plays no sound itself, CT-29): the cue is `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (semantics in CT-29, test in AC-CT-138); until Audio ships its asset the queued press stays the "documented reason" of CT-GF-2(1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. **Panel item state while a raise is queued from the panel** (Chart accepted, or Save & Quit refused into `UI3_PLATE`, within the interval of the last lower): the panel stays shown unchanged, all four items stay enabled, the bracket stays on the accepted item, and a repeat accept is idempotent; `cancel` cancels the queued raise first (the panel stays), and a second `cancel` closes the panel. The queue is cleared by any `request_restore` (TX-27). A queued raise has no hold or fill running, so nothing destructive is pending.
247	- **Scope.** The governor applies to the panel open (TX-13), the console-press chart open (TX-18; this supersedes the earlier "never to the console-press entry"), Chart from the panel (TX-16, TX-17) and the message-plate raises (TX-24, TX-25). It never delays the irreversible console press itself: a console press with a valid pick submits `pod_hop` at once and is not a layer raise (CT-10).
248	- **Value and derivation.** `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` = `ceil(1000 / FLASH_MAX_PER_S)` = 334 ms (registry `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, locked; same derivation as the registry's 334 ms floor for lying-readout ticks). With raises at least that far from the preceding lower, a rolling 1-s window holds at most three raises and so at most six opposing layer transitions, which scores `F <= 3` under the registry `flash_count` (Pipeline PR-13, D.15: `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)`). **Under reduce flashing** the interval is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` = 1000 ms (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 500-1500), so at most one raise per rolling second and `F <= 2`; with the long end of the fade band this is the toggle's real work. **Because reduce flashing is ON at first launch (user ruling D79, CT-19), 1000 ms is the interval every new player meets until they turn the toggle off**; the 334 ms interval is what a player who opts out, or a returning player who switched it off, gets. This is the price of the safe direction and is a playtest observable (OQ-CT-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The HUD's held-ON warning mark (HUD HS-23) is already solid under reduce flashing, so a pause adds no mark edge there.

278	**CT-7. The pick (`ChartPick`).**
279	*Rule.* `ChartPick` is NONE or one `derelict_id`. It is host-local presentation state of this layer: never simulation, never persisted, never a field of `web.state` or `web.view`, never assumed to depend on pause (WM-8, WM:1300). **Setting:** on the chart with `pod_at == HOME_ID` and `transit_state == IDLE`, accept (CT-5) on a legal target (CT-9) sets the pick, replacing any previous pick; accepting the already-picked node leaves it set (idempotent, so a double press cannot clear it by accident); accepting the HOME node (the origin) **clears** the pick; accepting a non-selectable node does nothing (**orchestrator ruling:** the ux-designer's rule; the ui-programmer's alternative, "accept on the picked node clears it, HOME is a no-op", was declined because a double press would clear the pick). The pick is shown by a Tungsten dashed planned-sortie line from the HOME node to the picked node (WM:1048 "planned sortie"), plus the bracket wherever focus is: a shape difference (dashed versus absent), so no colour carries it. A focused but unpicked node shows the bracket only and never a previewed route (a previewed route is a recommendation by default). Nothing else changes on the node: no label, no number (CT-14).

334	| planned sortie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | Tungsten dashed line = "the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight": from `ChartPick` (HOME to the pick, CT-7) or `pod_at` (pod node to HOME, CT-10) while `transit_state == IDLE`; from `leg_target_id` (HOME to the target) on an OUT leg and from `leg_origin_id` (the departure derelict to HOME) on a BACK leg, only in LEG / ARRIVING (CT-15); never in BERTHING *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G2)* | n/a | n/a |
335	
336	**The home-ship composite (the drawing rule for berthed and absorbed records)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) carries, per derelict record, a `home_attach` offset `(dx, dy)` in chart-local art px from HOME's centre to the record's centre, authored so the 24x24 glyph rectangles **share one full edge** (`|dx| = 24, dy = 0` or `dx = 0, |dy| = 24`); "the socket edge" of WM:1083 is that shared edge. The composite is drawn from the existing glyph assets, with no new asset: (a) **berthed**: the record's template glyph at the attach point plus the A17 seam quad on the shared edge; the record is **not** drawn at its authored position while berthed, and returns there on `unberth`; (b) **ABSORBED**: the same glyph at the same attach point in the HOME stroke style, with the seam replaced by the Ground erase quad; (c) the pod marker follows the drawn position of its record. **Berthed and absorbed records are excluded from the snap graph, from focus and from the pairwise `S_MIN` lint of their authored positions**, because they are not focusable; their attach rectangles are linted instead: each must not overlap any other node's bracket-padded rectangle, and HOME plus every attach rectangle must lie inside the chart frame (D.1b). The lint is re-run for each composite state of AC-CT-120: none, B berthed, B absorbed, A and B absorbed. If two records are given the same side of HOME the lint fails the build. Status is read from `web.view` on every change; a record whose status leaves ABSORBED or `berthed` (an `unberth`, or a restore) is simply drawn at its authored position again.
337	
338	**Per-state paint table for the composite** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Moment 4's only visible reward for the berth-and-weld loop, so "HOME stroke style" is defined here). Every glyph is painted in four layers, back to front: the Ground clearing (`NODE_CLEAR_PAD_PX`), the **interior fill**, the **silhouette stroke**, the **outline**; the seam and erase quads come last.
339	
340	| State | Interior fill | Silhouette stroke | Outline | Last quad |
341	|---|---|---|---|---|
342	| HOME | Ground | Graphite lit, 1 px (HOME's own stroke, the reference for "HOME stroke style") | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten point; no seam |
343	| UNSEEN | Ground | Graphite lit plain rectangle | 1-px Hull Grey | none |
344	| SEEN / BOARDED | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten tick if `unknown_seen` |
345	| `berthed` | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette, at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | solid 1-px **Hull Grey seam** quad on the shared edge (A17) |
346	| ABSORBED | Ground | **exactly HOME's stroke** (same colour and weight), at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | a **Ground erase quad** over every stroke and outline column of the shared edge (inset 1 art px at each end so the corners close); the erase repaints the **interior-fill colour (Ground)**, so the two interiors read as one and no seam is visible; no tick and no Tungsten point on the record |
347	| ORPHAN | Ground | Graphite mid | dashed 1-px Hull Grey | none |
348	
349	The fill and the erase colour are the same Ground, which is why the erase leaves no visible seam between two fills. The art-director signs the geometry of A1 to A3 and A17 (how many stroke and outline columns the shared edge carries) **before** any golden of AC-CT-120 is captured; the erase quad spans however many columns that geometry has.
350	State is never carried by colour alone: every state has a distinct silhouette or mark (tick, seam, detachment, glyph), satisfying SL:1010 and HR-10 by construction. Routes, seams and rule lines are 1-art-px quads aligned to whole art px, never width-1 line draws on a fractional transform (4.7 `CanvasItem` line drawing has no antialiasing feather; -> ADR candidate (b)).

## Detailed Design

### Core Rules

Rules are grouped by topic (A-H); ids are stable, not sequential within a group (CT-42 to CT-44 sit with the topic they belong to). Rule ids are `CT-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas); acceptance criteria `AC-CT-n` (Acceptance Criteria) and open questions `OQ-CT-n` (Open Questions). Each rule is stated as **Rule**, **Why**, **Source**. Where two specialist proposals differed and no earlier ruling decided it, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: ...)". Names that Web Map & Transit marks provisional (`web.view`, `web.state`, `transit_state`) are used with that mark carried (WM-36). `HOME_ID` := the `derelict_id` of the `web.view.nodes[]` entry whose `kind` is the home ship (the WM-3 roster `kind`); it is a derived label, never a constant and never registered (WM defines no such constant). Godot-specific mechanisms are not designed here: each is marked "-> ADR candidate" (ADRs (a)-(f) are listed at the end of the section), and anything the engine reference cannot source is marked NOT SOURCEABLE. **Engine reference coverage:** `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/rendering.md`, `VERSION.md` and `breaking-changes.md`; there is **no** `scripting.md` or `core.md`, and nothing on `ConfigFile`, `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode`, `Window` display-mode APIs, `Input.mouse_mode`, key-echo detection, focus-out notifications, font-importer flags or AccessKit property names; those are NOT SOURCEABLE and are routed to the ADRs below.

#### A. What the layer is

**CT-1. A meta layer, not a place.**
*Rule.* The chart table is one PIPE layer-3 `CanvasLayer` in the **root viewport**, opened by the `chart_table` input action (Esc / Start) from the `gameplay` context only (in the pod, on a derelict, in the home-ship). In `inspect_card` the same press is consumed by the Adapter: the card closes first, the context returns to `gameplay`, no event reaches this layer, no `request_pause` is made and no overlay opens, and a running channel is untouched (PC-2 context return table; AC-PCI-170); a second press, now in `gameplay`, opens the layer (TX-13 / TX-14, governed by CT-3). In `chat` (VS-B) the layer does not open *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*. It has no prop, no location, no lighting, no glow, no ambient, no occlusion and no camera jolt. It is scaled by the HUD scale `H` for the bitmap face and continuously for the reading face (PR-12).
*Why.* A prop would be a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and could lie; the meta layer is honest by definition (ART 7.0 row 3: "can a reading lie? never"). The chart must be reachable on a sortie, which a home-ship console could not be. An in-world "chart-table console" or ship schematic does not exist (IW-28, C4).
*Source.* PIPE:94-103 (PR-3); PC-2 (contexts and context return table); PCI:78; ART 7.0.

**CT-2. Truth channel.**
*Rule.* Layer 3 is never wrapped by the Perception Filter or by Sanity. No gleam, glide, tremor or settle occurs on any chart, panel or menu element (ART 7.3: the three motion signatures are readings only, and nothing on this layer is a reading). The layer is pixel-identical at sanity stage 0 and at forced stage 3, apart from the world visible beneath the panel. It never carries Violet or Flesh (ART 4.6), and Alarm Red appears on no element, because the layer draws no failing instrument (HR-4: red is never text). The only motion on the layer is the filament drift (CT-13, CT-40), the ART 7.3 cut/fade band and the ART 7.3 bracket ease-out, and the linear hold bar (CT-22).
*Why.* P1; ART HR-6 names menu, pause and settings layers as anchors; PF:223 (row 9, TRUTH: the pass sits below every `CanvasLayer`); SN:1226 (TRUTH anchor).
*Source.* PIPE PR-3 / PR-10; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-4, HR-6. **Note.** The world frozen or running under the panel keeps whatever it showed, including a lie (CT-4, Player Fantasy "Under hallucination"); the panel does not.

**CT-3. Surface architecture: panel first, stable order.**
*Rule.* `chart_table` opens the **panel**, a right-third plate over the world (ART 7.4). The panel has exactly four items in this fixed order: **Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit**. The order never changes with state. An item that cannot act is shown **disabled** (the disabled style of CT-VA-7: Hull Grey label and a dashed 1-px Hull Grey border, so it clears the 3:1 glyph floor by shape plus tone; it is no longer Graphite lit, which measured 2.8:1), never hidden *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Default focus on open is Resume (non-destructive). Chart (and any message plate) replaces the panel in a cut (a replacement is not an appearance, so it takes no fade), except under reduce flashing, where it uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band (`CHART_FADE_MS`, CT-13). A replacement that raises layer-3 coverage is a governed raise (the re-open governor below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. "Display & Comfort" opens its page inside the panel's column. The panel carries only item labels and the empty status-line slot that holds `FAILED` when a write fails (CT-17, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); every paragraph of copy lives on a full-bleed **message plate** on the chart-table register (CT-28).
*Why.* One entry point; the world stays visible under the panel as ART 7.4 specifies; the HUD (layer 2) stays visible and frozen behind the pause panel, except that an active warning mark is held ON solid (HUD HS-23; the HUD's rule, acknowledged here; the full-bleed chart covers layer 2 entirely); a stable order is a muscle-memory affordance and menu layers are anchors that must not shift (HR-6). The accepted cost is that the chart is two actions from a pause; CT-10 (a no-pick console press opens the chart) offsets it. A second `chart` action stays an Alpha playtest fallback owned by the Player Controller and is not designed here.
*Ruled (HR-13, ASK-CT-8, OQ-CT-15, OQ-CT-27): the re-open governor. A player-initiated toggle of a large plate counts toward the 3 Hz ceiling, and the layer and the kernel are rate-limited together, never the picture alone* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director ruling)*.
- **Coverage levels.** `c = 0` CLOSED; `c = 1` the panel family (`PANEL`, `SAVE_FAILED`, `DISPLAY_COMFORT` opened from the panel); `c = 2` any full-bleed in-session plate (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`). A **raise** is a transition that increases `c` (TX-13, TX-14, TX-16, TX-17, TX-18, TX-24, TX-25); a **lower** decreases it (TX-15, TX-19, TX-35). Boot-flow screens are not governed (no world is visible under them and they appear once per process).
- **Close and resume are never delayed.** Every lower takes effect on the press frame. In SOLO a close calls `request_resume` on that frame.
- **A raise that comes less than `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` after the most recent lower is queued** and applied the first presented frame at or after `t_last_lower + CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` on the layer's UI clock (CT-43). A raise with no lower in the preceding interval is applied at once (the first open after a quiet period is never delayed). A queued raise applies **as one unit**: the plate, the focus, and in SOLO the `request_pause` of a CLOSED-to-PANEL or CLOSED-to-CHART raise happen on the same frame, so the picture and the kernel state always match (a queued open leaves the layer CLOSED and the kernel `RUNNING`; it never leaves an opaque plate over a running sim, nor a paused sim with no plate).
- **The queue is latched, one slot, and cancellable.** The pressed intent is held even if the key is released before the interval ends; there is one slot (the latest desired raise replaces an earlier queued one); only a `cancel` press while a raise is queued **cancels** it (the layer stays at its current level and a CLOSED layer is never opened and never paused) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: **a repeat `chart_table` press while a raise is queued is idempotent** (the raise stays queued, the latch is unchanged, nothing else happens), because at the first-launch default the lag is 1,000 ms and a player who pauses within a second of resuming (Moment 2, an emergency action) presses Esc twice from impatience and must not end up unpaused. **Queued acknowledgement:** the queue gives an audio-only acknowledgement (a single cue, no visual element, so no flash risk) requested from Adaptive Audio (ASK-CT-20; the layer plays no sound itself, CT-29): the cue is `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (semantics in CT-29, test in AC-CT-138); until Audio ships its asset the queued press stays the "documented reason" of CT-GF-2(1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. **Panel item state while a raise is queued from the panel** (Chart accepted, or Save & Quit refused into `UI3_PLATE`, within the interval of the last lower): the panel stays shown unchanged, all four items stay enabled, the bracket stays on the accepted item, and a repeat accept is idempotent; `cancel` cancels the queued raise first (the panel stays), and a second `cancel` closes the panel. The queue is cleared by any `request_restore` (TX-27). A queued raise has no hold or fill running, so nothing destructive is pending.
- **Scope.** The governor applies to the panel open (TX-13), the console-press chart open (TX-18; this supersedes the earlier "never to the console-press entry"), Chart from the panel (TX-16, TX-17) and the message-plate raises (TX-24, TX-25). It never delays the irreversible console press itself: a console press with a valid pick submits `pod_hop` at once and is not a layer raise (CT-10).
- **Value and derivation.** `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` = `ceil(1000 / FLASH_MAX_PER_S)` = 334 ms (registry `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, locked; same derivation as the registry's 334 ms floor for lying-readout ticks). With raises at least that far from the preceding lower, a rolling 1-s window holds at most three raises and so at most six opposing layer transitions, which scores `F <= 3` under the registry `flash_count` (Pipeline PR-13, D.15: `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)`). **Under reduce flashing** the interval is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` = 1000 ms (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 500-1500), so at most one raise per rolling second and `F <= 2`; with the long end of the fade band this is the toggle's real work. **Because reduce flashing is ON at first launch (user ruling D79, CT-19), 1000 ms is the interval every new player meets until they turn the toggle off**; the 334 ms interval is what a player who opts out, or a returning player who switched it off, gets. This is the price of the safe direction and is a playtest observable (OQ-CT-29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The HUD's held-ON warning mark (HUD HS-23) is already solid under reduce flashing, so a pause adds no mark edge there.
- **Metric, defined once.** This GDD does not define a flash metric. The ceiling is the Pipeline's registry `flash_count` evaluated over the layer-3 rectangle and the frame mean from a per-frame linear-luminance log (acceptance AC-CT-115), on a bright lamp-lit fixture and on a fixture with an active held-ON warning mark, with the HUD mark edges counted in the same capture. If that capture shows `F > 3` on the mark's grid cell at 334 ms, the interval rises (range 334-1000) before the story closes.
- **Accepted cost, stated plainly.** A re-open pressed within the interval of a close leaves the world running with no plate for up to 334 ms (1000 ms under reduce flashing). This is the price of keeping picture and kernel together; the alternative of an immediate kernel pause with a coalesced picture was rejected because it can leave an opaque plate over a running sim or a paused sim with no plate (CT-GF-2 "Answered"). The PauseGate-deferred-resume alternative is **not adopted**: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the ruled form (layer and kernel rate-limited together, a close never delayed, a re-open queued and applied with its pause) stands (OQ-CT-28, D78) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
*Source.* ART 7.4, HR-6, HR-13; PCI:78; Pipeline PR-13, registry `flash_count` and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`.

**CT-4. PauseGate (answers KRN Open Question 6).**
*Rule.* One adapter, `PauseGate`, with two modes. **SOLO (MVP):** opening the layer calls `request_pause`; closing it calls `request_resume` (KRN CR-15; PCI:147). **OVERLAY (VS-B, reserved):** no kernel call; the kernel stays `RUNNING`; panel and chart are identical. **No chart, pick, panel or menu rule may read `kernel.state == PAUSED`**; `PauseGate.mode` is the one place SOLO and OVERLAY differ. The single exception is inside `PauseGate` itself: it exposes one boolean, `can_save_quit`, true only when the mode is SOLO **and** the kernel reports `PAUSED` (Save/Load's `PAUSED -> SAVING`, SL-6, needs it); nothing else on the layer reads it except the Save & Quit item's enabled state. In OVERLAY `can_save_quit` is replaced by Session / Save-Load's form (`saveload.request_save`, reserved, SL:37, SL-17). Verbatim answer to KRN:961: **The Chart Table does not assume "pick a target" happens while paused.** The pick is a host-local selection valid with the kernel `RUNNING` or `PAUSED`; nothing depends on time standing still.
*Timing.* The layer enters PANEL on the press frame, or on the frame the re-open governor releases a queued raise (CT-3), whichever applies (presentation does not wait on the kernel); the kernel honours the control-plane request at the next boundary (CR-15, amended: the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service) and is `PAUSED` up to one tick later; the fade (`CHART_FADE_MS`, inside the ART 7.3 band) hides the gap, and `can_save_quit` is false until the kernel confirms. A same-boundary `request_pause` then `request_resume` (a double press) must leave no wedged half-open state: the layer keeps its own `open` boolean and `PauseGate` re-issues the latest desired state until the kernel matches (host-local, no commands). The kernel applies a same-boundary pair in arrival order, never coalesced, and ends `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle (CR-15 as amended 2026-10-27; ASK-CT-9 is answered), which is exactly the case the re-issue rule covers (a double press from a quiet start is an open then an immediate close; a double press within the governor interval after a close queues one raise and the second press is idempotent: nothing is sent until the interval ends, one `request_pause` then goes out with the plate, and only `cancel` clears the queue, CT-3, AC-CT-114c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to CT-3 and AC-CT-114c)*.
*Why.* KRN CR-16: pause is single-player only; in co-op a menu cannot stop a shared sim. Reading kernel state anywhere else is the divergence the brief's risk R4 warns about. The pause is available during a leg and during `TRANSIT_HOLD` and "changes nothing" there (WM:1268).
*Source.* KRN CR-15, CR-16, KRN:129, KRN:961; PCI:147; SL-6. **-> ADR candidate (a):** the relationship between kernel `PAUSED` and `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode` of layer 3 is NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference. Behavioural requirement stated here: layer 3 handles input and animates on its own UI clock (CT-43) while the kernel is `PAUSED`.

**CT-5. Input depth: Esc closes, cancel steps back.**
*Rule.* In the `chart_table` context (PC-2 sends `set_move_intent {NONE}`, clears the run latch, **submits `cancel_channel`** for a hold-mode channel, and releases the cursor):
- `chart_table` (Esc / Start) is a toggle and **closes the whole layer from any depth** (SOLO then calls `request_resume`).
- A `chart_table` press made in `inspect_card` never reaches the layer (the Adapter closes the card, PC-2 context return table); every toggle rule in this section concerns a press in `gameplay` or inside the layer *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*.
- `cancel` (X / B) **steps back one level**: Display & Comfort, Chart or a message plate returns to the panel; the panel closes (PCI:73, "closes the current UI"). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:)* a chart opened by a console press has no panel behind it, so `cancel` returns it to `CLOSED` (TX-35); Display & Comfort opened from the main menu returns to the main menu (TX-37).
- **Hold exception (orchestrator ruling: the stricter, safer reading of the rulings).** While a hold-to-confirm fill is running (CT-22), release, `cancel` **or** `chart_table` aborts the fill (the bar snaps to empty in the same frame) and **nothing else happens in that press**; a second `chart_table` press then closes the layer. The alternative (Esc during a fill aborts and also closes) was proposed and declined: an Esc that resumes the simulation while a destructive hold was in progress is a second effect from one press.
- On boot-flow screens (notice, main menu, Display & Comfort opened from the menu, UI-5, UI-8, UI-9) `chart_table` does nothing **except abort a running hold fill (TX-10)**, and `cancel` goes back only where a previous boot screen exists (UI-5 to the main menu; UI-8 and UI-9 have none).
- During a Save & Quit write (CT-21, state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`) `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored so a half-written state is never abandoned.
- `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` are **not** actions of the `chart_table` context: the Controller emits the zoom edges from `gameplay` and `inspect_card` only (PC-2 context table; PCI source-scan criterion), so no zoom edge reaches the layer, and the wheel, `=` and `-` keys are not zoom here. No zoom row, hint or glyph appears on any surface (zoom is never a setting, PIPE:232). The mouse wheel scrolls in this context (legal across contexts); nothing scrolls at MVP *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "a zoom press is discarded by the layer" is stale; the D-pad is navigation, CT-45)*.
- **Directional navigation, accept, back and close come from the Adapter's MenuInput feed (CT-45)**, not from the layer reading devices: the four-way cardinal read, the deadzone hysteresis (`MOVE_DEADZONE` / `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, PCI, not registered), echo suppression and the latch on a closing control are the Adapter's. The per-device navigation set is stick, D-pad, arrow keys and WASD; accept is the physical controls of `interact` in this context (E, gamepad A, plus Enter and Space), **never a mouse button** (the Controller's `chart_table` note excludes every mouse button, PC-2a, ASK-CT-15 answered, C23 resolved) (a click is a `POINTER` event, CT-45) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*; back is `cancel` (X / B); close is `chart_table` (Esc / Start). The Controller's `chart_table`-context note (PCI default bindings) accepts the reuse of the `move_*` and `interact` physical controls and adds no action (ASK-CT-2 is answered for the reuse; the Enter and Space accept bindings and the LMB exclusion are in PC-2a). A rebind that removes the last path to the chart table on the active device is refused `BINDING_REQUIRED{chart_table}` by the Controller's side *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
*Source.* PCI:62, :73-80, :699; PIPE:688, 232.

**CT-6. Focus is a shape; dual focus.**
*Rule.* Focus is the Tungsten bracket (left bar plus chamfer corners) **and** a one-art-px thickening of the focused bezel; never a Tungsten fill (ART 7.2, HR-11). The bracket relocates with a 100 ms ease-out (ART 7.3). The bracket is drawn from **keyboard / gamepad focus only**: it hides on mouse motion and is revealed again by the FIRST key or pad navigation press after that motion, which only reveals it on the retained focus and moves nothing; the next press navigates (CT-45 (c); PCI PC-13) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Mouse hover turns the item's label Tungsten (ART 7.4) and never moves the bracket; a chart node carries no label, so hover changes nothing on the node itself, the **pointer cursor changes shape over a selectable node only** (no art, no label; OQ-CT-9 closed) and the click's visible result is the route (CT-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A mouse click on an item activates it and moves key/pad focus to it, so the next pad press navigates from where the mouse acted; the bracket stays hidden until key or pad input. Glyphs follow the last device with `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` (PCI, registry; value in Tuning Knobs); mixed input is permitted. Every flow is gamepad-complete (HR-14). A click on an item is activated only when the pointer-up lands on the item that received the press.
*Why.* Godot 4.6 split mouse/touch focus from keyboard/gamepad focus (`modules/ui.md`, HIGH risk, "test with BOTH"): the bracket must be drawn from the keyboard/gamepad focus and not from hover or PC-13 cannot hold. Both paths are tested (Acceptance Criteria).
*Source.* ART 7.2, 7.3, 7.4; PCI:141 (PC-13); HR-11, HR-14; `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`.

#### B. The pick and the sortie

**CT-7. The pick (`ChartPick`).**
*Rule.* `ChartPick` is NONE or one `derelict_id`. It is host-local presentation state of this layer: never simulation, never persisted, never a field of `web.state` or `web.view`, never assumed to depend on pause (WM-8, WM:1300). **Setting:** on the chart with `pod_at == HOME_ID` and `transit_state == IDLE`, accept (CT-5) on a legal target (CT-9) sets the pick, replacing any previous pick; accepting the already-picked node leaves it set (idempotent, so a double press cannot clear it by accident); accepting the HOME node (the origin) **clears** the pick; accepting a non-selectable node does nothing (**orchestrator ruling:** the ux-designer's rule; the ui-programmer's alternative, "accept on the picked node clears it, HOME is a no-op", was declined because a double press would clear the pick). Closing the chart or the layer **keeps** the pick. The pick is shown by a Tungsten dashed planned-sortie line from the HOME node to the picked node (WM:1048 "planned sortie"), plus the bracket wherever focus is: a shape difference (dashed versus absent), so no colour carries it. A focused but unpicked node shows the bracket only and never a previewed route (a previewed route is a recommendation by default). Nothing else changes on the node: no label, no number (CT-14).
*Why.* The pick is "the deliberate step" (WM:1225); the console press is the commitment (CT-10). Focus and pick are two states, so the player needs a non-colour way to see "picked" while the bracket sits elsewhere. The Tungsten dashed line **always means "the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight"** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `transit_state == IDLE` it is the target the next console press carries (HOME to `ChartPick` when the pod is at HOME, the pod's node to HOME when it is at a derelict); on an OUT leg, only in LEG and ARRIVING, it runs HOME to `web.view.leg_target_id` and confirms what the player committed to (CT-15; it never reads `ChartPick`); on a BACK leg, only in LEG and ARRIVING, it runs from `web.view.leg_origin_id` to HOME (the same line as the IDLE line from a derelict to HOME, CT-10), and it is **never** drawn in BERTHING *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G2)*. It is not a recommendation (from a derelict it is the only legal move; from HOME it appears only after the player's own pick), and this single definition closes OQ-CT-10 (the route is the pick mark; no second mark).
*Source.* WM-8 (WM:203), WM:1225, WM:1300.

**CT-8. Pick lifecycle.**
*Rule.* `ChartPick := NONE` on: (1) any `request_restore`, for every `restore_reason` (`NEW_GAME`, `LOAD_GAME`, `DEATH_STUB`, `FAULT_RECOVERY`; SL-21); (2) arrival (`POD_ARRIVED`, WM-31), detected equivalently as `pod_at` leaving `IN_FLIGHT` so a test double needs no event bus; (3) whenever the picked record leaves the legal-target mirror (ABSORBED, ORPHAN, `berthed`, or absent from `web.view`). The pick is revalidated against `web.view` on every chart open and every `web.view` change. It is **frozen** (not editable) while `transit_state != IDLE`. No rule reads it except the console seam (CT-10). If the node holding key/pad focus leaves the selectable set, focus moves to HOME; the bracket otherwise does not move and no message is shown.
*Why.* A stale pick is the only way the chart and the press can disagree. The sim still validates with Web Map & Transit's own reasons (`TARGET_UNKNOWN`, `TARGET_ABSORBED`, `TARGET_BERTHED`, `BERTH_PENDING`; WM-9), which this GDD cites and never re-lists as its own.
*Source.* WM-9 (WM:205-217), WM-31; SL-21.

**CT-9. Legal-target mirror.**
*Rule.* The chart computes `legal_targets` (D.4) purely from `web.view`, for **selectability only**: from HOME, derelicts whose `status` is not ABSORBED or ORPHAN and that are not `berthed`, **and none at all while any record is `berthed` and not ABSORBED** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Web Map's E-36 refuses every hop with `BERTH_PENDING` or `TARGET_BERTHED` then, and `berthed` is already a `web.view` field the chart reads, so an offered choice that cannot succeed is not offered); from a derelict, only HOME; with `transit_state != IDLE` or `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT`, none. UNSEEN derelicts are selectable bare nodes (WM:1299; OQ-WM-4). ORPHAN is drawn but neither focusable nor selectable (WM:1046). The mirror is **not a validation and not a second copy of WM-9's reason order**; every refusal is Web Map & Transit's and Interaction's, shown as words on the register plate (not here). **The mirror never reflects `FUEL_LOW`, `BUSY`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` or `CAPACITY`**; those refusals are words at the console only (CT-35). `BERTH_PENDING` is reflected only as the empty set while a record is berthed (below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **The one berth-driven emptiness** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while a record is `berthed` and not ABSORBED, `legal_targets` is `{}` from HOME (a `web.view` read, not a copy of WM-9's reason order); the chart still opens from the panel, every node is non-focusable except HOME, and no route can be drawn; the words explaining why are Web Map's `BERTH_PENDING` words on the register plate at the console (CT-10 R6), not text on the chart (OQ-CT-3).
*Why.* WM-9 defines `TARGET_ABSORBED` (WM:217) as "a welded-in or orphaned record; the Chart Table never offers it", so that reason already covers ORPHAN, and WM:1046 draws ORPHAN not selectable; the mirror is what makes "never offers" true. Greying a node on low fuel would put a fuel meter on the truth layer, which is why the exclusion above is a named sentence (CT-35).
*Source.* WM-4 (WM:193); WM-9 (WM:205-217).

**CT-10. The console seam: the only simulation write.**
*Rule.* The chart submits nothing. The **pod console press** (Interaction's CONSOLE subject, `tool_required` NONE) is the only simulation write and the only commitment (WM:1225, WM:1301): no "confirm sortie", no resume-and-hop gesture, no confirmation dialog anywhere on this layer. Resolution at the press, in the Input Adapter's seam:
1. **From a derelict:** HOME is implied (WM-4, WM-8: "from a derelict the press carries HOME implicitly"). If the chart is opened there it shows the bracket on HOME as the only focusable node, and the planned-sortie line from the pod's node to HOME is drawn from `pod_at` (not from `ChartPick`), because that is the only legal move; the selection cannot move to another node. This implied line carries the same single meaning as CT-7's dashed line (the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `transit_state == IDLE` it is the target the next console press carries; the in-flight route (either leg) is CT-15's; it is not a recommendation.
2. **From HOME with a valid pick:** the press submits `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` at the POD prompt, or `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` at the DOCK prompt (WM-21). Which of the two a press means is decided by **which prompt was pressed** (the verb-resolution table below), never by a mode of the chart.
3. **From HOME with no valid pick, at a prompt that needs a pick (`pod_hop`, `berth`):** the press **opens the chart** (host-local, no refusal, no simulation effect), **even when exactly one legal target exists**: an auto-implied hop from HOME would make the press both choice and commitment. Default focus on opening is the pod's own node (HOME), never a target, so focus is never a recommendation. In SOLO the open requests a pause as in CT-4 and is a governed raise (CT-3). **This rule applies only to `pod_hop` and `berth`; `unberth` takes no payload, never needs a pick and is never swallowed by it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
4. **Verb-resolution table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; keyed on the facts the Adapter can read at the press: `pod_at`, `transit_state`, whether a record is `berthed`, and `ChartPick`; the prompt is the Interaction subject that was pressed)*. Console preconditions that are Interaction's and Web Map's (in reach, lit, `console_ready`) are evaluated first and answered in words on the register plate; the table starts after them.

| Row | `pod_at` | `transit_state` | `berthed` record | `ChartPick` | Prompt pressed | Result of the press |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | a derelict | IDLE | n/a (berth starts only from HOME) | not read | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := HOME_ID}` (HOME is implied, WM-4, WM-8) |
| R1b *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a derelict | IDLE | n/a | not read | DOCK | **no DOCK prompt exists there** (WM-21: `berth` starts only from HOME; the DOCK subject exists in the home airlock only, IA-40; no DOCK subject exists at a derelict dock); through a test double Web Map answers `NOT_DOCKED_HERE` and the press submits no command and opens no chart *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| R2 | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` |
| R3 | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | POD | opens the chart (entry origin `CONSOLE`, TX-18); no command |
| R4a | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | DOCK | `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` |
| R4b | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | DOCK | opens the chart (as R3) |
| R5 | HOME | IDLE | a record B | **not read** | DOCK | `unberth{}` (no payload; the DOCK prompt's verb is `unberth` while a record is berthed; never opens the chart) |
| R6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | HOME | IDLE | a record B (not ABSORBED) | not read (`legal_targets` is `{}`, so a pick is always invalid) | POD | **no chart opens and no `pod_hop{target}` is built from the pick**; the press is routed to Web Map so the register plate shows its `BERTH_PENDING` words (WM-9: a payload-less `pod_hop` while an unwelded derelict is berthed returns `BERTH_PENDING`, ordered before `TARGET_UNKNOWN`; AC-WM-139); the layer renders no words *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| R7 | any | LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING | any | not read | either | no command and no chart: the refusal words are Web Map's (`IN_TRANSIT`, `BUSY`), shown on the register plate |
| R8 | `IN_FLIGHT` | any | any | not read | none exists | no console can be pressed |

The POD prompt and the DOCK prompt are **two Interaction CONSOLE subjects, POD_CONSOLE and DOCK_CONSOLE, told apart by Layout's `console_role`** (IA-40; the DOCK subject exists in the home airlock only), because pod at HOME, nothing berthed and a valid pick leave both `pod_hop{pick}` and `berth{pick}` legal, and one `interact` cannot mean both. The split and the table are **agreed 2026-10-28**: Interaction IA-40 (split, DOCK rows `unberth` priority 1 eligible iff `berthed_present()`, `berth` priority 2), Layout LY-23 (`console_role`), Web Map WM-8 / WM-9 (ASK-CT-13, answered) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The prompt wording stays state-neutral (IA-40) and never names a target, distance or cost.
5. **Stale-pick echo (drawn by Interaction; ASK-CT-14 ANSWERED 2026-10-28, no longer a gate item)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The echo is drawn by Interaction from this system's host-local read `pick_glyph_key` (the node glyph key the chart draws for the pick; HOME's at a derelict POD press); this system publishes that read and nothing else. Because the pick is invisible at the console and the hop has no confirm, the POD and DOCK plates carry a small text-free echo of the pick (**at R1, from a derelict, the echo is HOME's node glyph**, so the player sees what the irreversible press carries; at R2 and R4a it is the pick's): the pick's node glyph as the chart draws it (the plain rectangle, the Foundry silhouette and, if seen, the tick), nothing else; no name, no ordinal, no distance, no cost (G6 and the CT-44 exception are unchanged). A clear-after-N-seconds timer is rejected (a timeout would change what a press means without the player acting). A playtest observable records presses made with a stale pick (CT-GF-12). Re-opening the chart with focus on the existing pick was considered and **not adopted** (default focus stays HOME; the UX spec may revisit it).
The seam (the Adapter injects the host-local pick into the payload at R2 and R4a; a no-pick press at R3 and R4b routes to "open chart") is **accepted** by the Controller (PCI:100 and Interactions row 17) and by Interaction (IA-40) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "provisional" and "degraded if refused" retired; ASK-CT-1 is answered; ASK-CT-13 and ASK-CT-14 were the new asks, both ANSWERED 2026-10-28)*.
*Why.* P2 (the commitment at the console, not on a menu); WM-8; an irreversible, fuel-costing write that depends on a hidden host-local pick needs its resolution stated per fact. *Source.* WM-8, WM-21, WM-22, WM:1225, WM:1301; IA-40; PCI Interactions row 17. **-> ADR candidate (d):** the pick-to-console submit seam.

#### C. Drawing the web

**CT-11. Drawing `web.view` (the twelve rows, owned layout).**
*Rule.* The chart draws `web.view` exactly per WM section 3 (WM:1036-1050); this GDD owns the layout and Web Map & Transit owns the drawing grammar. The summary below restates the grammar only to bind the layout; colours and silhouettes are WM's and ART 4.6's.

| `web.view` fact | Drawn as | Focusable | Selectable |
|---|---|---|---|
| HOME node | Tungsten fixture point + 1-px rectilinear Foundry silhouette (`ui_glyph_node_home_24`) | yes (origin; start focus when `pod_at == HOME_ID`) | no (origin; accept clears the pick, CT-7) |
| UNSEEN derelict | plain Graphite-lit rectangle (`ui_glyph_node_wreck_plain_24`), no dialect, no tick, no label | yes | yes |
| SEEN / BOARDED | Graphite-lit rectilinear silhouette chosen by `template_id` (`ui_glyph_node_wreck_foundry_24` at MVP) | yes | yes |
| `unknown_seen` | one 1-art-px square Tungsten tick inside the silhouette, 1-px Ground clearing, no glow, no circle | n/a | n/a |
| `berthed` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the record's own template glyph drawn **at its attach point** `HOME_pos + home_attach(record)` (below), not at its authored position, so it abuts HOME on the shared edge ("the socket edge"); a solid 1-px Hull Grey seam quad on that edge (A17), which reads as a join thicker than any 1-px outline (two strokes plus the seam) | no | no |
| ABSORBED *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the record's own template glyph at the **same attach point**, drawn in the HOME glyph's stroke style with no Tungsten point and no tick, and the **seam removed**: a Ground erase quad covers the two stroke columns of the shared edge (inset 1 art px at each end so the corners still close), so the two rectangles read as one silhouette | no | no |
| ORPHAN | Graphite mid, detached (at its authored position), dashed Hull Grey 1-px outline (CT-VA-8), no tick | no | no |
| `pod_at` HOME / a derelict | small rectilinear pod marker (`ui_glyph_pod_24`) at the **drawn position** of the record named by `pod_at` (its attach point if that record is berthed or absorbed; OQ-CT-21 closed: the case is unreachable at MVP, WM-21 needs `pod_at == HOME` and a hop to a berthed record is `TARGET_BERTHED`) | n/a | n/a |
| `pod_at` IN_FLIGHT | **no marker**; state word `IN TRANSIT` (CT-15) | n/a | n/a |
| planned sortie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | Tungsten dashed line = "the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight": from `ChartPick` (HOME to the pick, CT-7) or `pod_at` (pod node to HOME, CT-10) while `transit_state == IDLE`; from `leg_target_id` (HOME to the target) on an OUT leg and from `leg_origin_id` (the departure derelict to HOME) on a BACK leg, only in LEG / ARRIVING (CT-15); never in BERTHING *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G2)* | n/a | n/a |

**The home-ship composite (the drawing rule for berthed and absorbed records)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) carries, per derelict record, a `home_attach` offset `(dx, dy)` in chart-local art px from HOME's centre to the record's centre, authored so the 24x24 glyph rectangles **share one full edge** (`|dx| = 24, dy = 0` or `dx = 0, |dy| = 24`); "the socket edge" of WM:1083 is that shared edge. The composite is drawn from the existing glyph assets, with no new asset: (a) **berthed**: the record's template glyph at the attach point plus the A17 seam quad on the shared edge; the record is **not** drawn at its authored position while berthed, and returns there on `unberth`; (b) **ABSORBED**: the same glyph at the same attach point in the HOME stroke style, with the seam replaced by the Ground erase quad; (c) the pod marker follows the drawn position of its record. **Berthed and absorbed records are excluded from the snap graph, from focus and from the pairwise `S_MIN` lint of their authored positions**, because they are not focusable; their attach rectangles are linted instead: each must not overlap any other node's bracket-padded rectangle, and HOME plus every attach rectangle must lie inside the chart frame (D.1b). The lint is re-run for each composite state of AC-CT-120: none, B berthed, B absorbed, A and B absorbed. If two records are given the same side of HOME the lint fails the build. Status is read from `web.view` on every change; a record whose status leaves ABSORBED or `berthed` (an `unberth`, or a restore) is simply drawn at its authored position again.

**Per-state paint table for the composite** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Moment 4's only visible reward for the berth-and-weld loop, so "HOME stroke style" is defined here). Every glyph is painted in four layers, back to front: the Ground clearing (`NODE_CLEAR_PAD_PX`), the **interior fill**, the **silhouette stroke**, the **outline**; the seam and erase quads come last.

| State | Interior fill | Silhouette stroke | Outline | Last quad |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HOME | Ground | Graphite lit, 1 px (HOME's own stroke, the reference for "HOME stroke style") | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten point; no seam |
| UNSEEN | Ground | Graphite lit plain rectangle | 1-px Hull Grey | none |
| SEEN / BOARDED | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten tick if `unknown_seen` |
| `berthed` | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette, at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | solid 1-px **Hull Grey seam** quad on the shared edge (A17) |
| ABSORBED | Ground | **exactly HOME's stroke** (same colour and weight), at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | a **Ground erase quad** over every stroke and outline column of the shared edge (inset 1 art px at each end so the corners close); the erase repaints the **interior-fill colour (Ground)**, so the two interiors read as one and no seam is visible; no tick and no Tungsten point on the record |
| ORPHAN | Ground | Graphite mid | dashed 1-px Hull Grey | none |

The fill and the erase colour are the same Ground, which is why the erase leaves no visible seam between two fills. The art-director signs the geometry of A1 to A3 and A17 (how many stroke and outline columns the shared edge carries) **before** any golden of AC-CT-120 is captured; the erase quad spans however many columns that geometry has.
State is never carried by colour alone: every state has a distinct silhouette or mark (tick, seam, detachment, glyph), satisfying SL:1010 and HR-10 by construction. Routes, seams and rule lines are 1-art-px quads aligned to whole art px, never width-1 line draws on a fractional transform (4.7 `CanvasItem` line drawing has no antialiasing feather; -> ADR candidate (b)).

379	#### D. The panel, settings and the notice
380	
381	**CT-17. The pause panel's content.**
382	*Rule* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Save/Load's UI-2 was amended the same day to "no save fact on the pause panel"; the newest-record line, the playtime of the newest generation, is on the main-menu Continue screen only, read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, because pausing is free and a line that changed between writes would show that a write is overdue)*. The panel shows the four items of CT-3 and **no save fact**: no playtime, no depth label, no countdown, no "time since", no gate state, no per-write mark (SL UI-2, AC-SL-133). Its content is identical across any number of autosave periods. It reserves one **status-line slot** (height `PANEL_RECORD_LINE_H_HUD`, id retained for continuity, D.1) that is **empty** except in `SAVE_FAILED`, where it holds the plain word `FAILED` (CT-21); because the slot's presence is constant, opening the panel never reflows. The panel has **no title and no state word**: it never says "Paused" (in OVERLAY the sim is running, and a word that is false in one mode is a lie on the truth layer). `SaveInfo.depth_label` does **not** appear on the panel (it is on the main-menu Continue line only; the Web Map & Transit row at WM:1309 saying "pause panel / save list" is satisfied by the save list, routed as C13). Panel plate: opaque Ground (HR-2), one chamfered Graphite-lit border, one rivet mark per corner (ART 7.4). The world beneath is frozen exactly as lit, not dimmed, blurred or desaturated (PIPE:265); a click on that world does nothing (CT-41). Panel item labels are in the reading face (ART 7.1 assigns settings and long menu copy to the reading face; panel item labels follow it as menu copy, orchestrator ruling closing ASK-UP-3; a clarification row to the art-bible owner); the `FAILED` word and the Continue line's numerals are the instrument face.
383	*Source.* SL UI-2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, UI-4; ART 7.4; PIPE:265; WM:1309.

385	**CT-18. Display & Comfort page: exactly four controls.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
386	*Rule.* One page inside the panel's column (in-session) or the main menu's content column (boot-flow, from the Display & Comfort item of CT-23; the same S6, TX-36, TX-37) with four controls *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; master volume added 2026-10-27, user rulings)*: **display mode** (windowed / fullscreen / borderless), **reduced motion**, **reduce flashing** and **master volume**. Defaults *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: display mode and reduced motion are the pipeline hooks' defaults (PR-13; PIPE:301 "MVP exposes the hooks with defaults"); **reduce flashing is ON at first launch** (user ruling D79, OQ-CT-7, CT-19); master volume starts at its top step, which Adaptive Audio's master bus treats as unity (Adaptive Audio's call, CT-29). Display mode is a three-choice list whose current choice is marked by a shape plus a word (not colour alone); the two booleans are chamfered switches (ART 7.4) with an on/off **word**. **Master volume** *(Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D85)*: a single row holding a **stepped control** of `VOLUME_STEPS` notches (10 at authoring, `[PLACEHOLDER]`; a stepped control and not a continuous slider so that a gamepad has exact steps, the same reason display mode is a list): Left / Right (the MenuInput directional feed, repeating by D.9) or a pointer click on a notch changes it by one step, the current step is marked by a shape plus a numeral (not colour alone), and step 0 is a legal choice (muted) shown with its numeral and no warning. The page publishes the step through the store's change signal; Adaptive Audio maps step to master-bus gain (the law, the floor and the default are its own; this layer carries no dB figure and plays no sound of its own, CT-29). It is not a safety toggle, so it is debounced like display mode (CT-19). Changes apply immediately and persist (CT-19); there is **no Apply button and no revert countdown** (a countdown would be a timer surface; any revert-on-failure safety is Settings' / an ADR). After a display-mode change the page reads back and shows the **applied** mode (a failed fullscreen request shows windowed); a mode change resizes the window, so `k`, `H_default`, the canvas and the panel width recompute live, the page stays open and focus is retained **by item id**, the bracket does not nudge and no animation plays on the relayout. The page carries only labels, switches and their words; it has no explanatory paragraphs. **Never on any page:** zoom (PIPE:232), rebinding, resolution list, world scale, **HUD scale** (deferred to Settings & Input Rebinding, Alpha: `H_default` already meets the 21-px floor on every display by construction), frame cap, V-sync, audio other than the one master volume control, the HR-15 ambient step (Lighting's), any true-value overlay (never an accessibility option, ART 7.4). Master volume is the fourth control (OQ-CT-1: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): added at MVP, D85) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The page's height is re-derived in D.1c.
387	*Why.* The first three controls (display mode, reduced motion, reduce flashing) are those an outside playtester needs and that PR-13(c)/(e) makes load-bearing; each is a boolean or enum hook the pipeline already defines. Master volume is the fourth because Display & Comfort is now reachable from the main menu (CT-23), so a first-time player can open the page before any world exists and would otherwise find no audio control at all *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. `Window` display-mode behaviour and failure reporting are NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference.
388	*Source.* PIPE PR-13, PR-14 (PIPE:228, 232), PIPE:301; ART 7.4.

390	**CT-19. Settings store.**
391	*Rule.* The four comfort values (display mode, reduced motion, reduce flashing, master volume) and the `notice_seen` flag *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* live in a host-local, per-install `SettingsStore` seam: **not a kernel block, not a command, not WORLD or PROFILE scope** (PROFILE is per-campaign, SL-9; settings survive New campaign). Nothing in the simulation reads it (HR-6: "no game state may read or alter" anchors, PCI:845). Consumers (Lighting, the Filter, Audio, the Camera) read `reduced_motion` and `reduce_flashing` through the store's read interface and a presentation-only change signal. A missing or unreadable store is treated as first launch with the first-launch defaults (reduce flashing ON, reduced motion at the pipeline default, master volume at its top step) and the notice (CT-20) is shown again (the safe direction) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* **The safety toggles (reduced motion, reduce flashing) and `notice_seen` are written synchronously on the change**, before the next presented frame, so a crash or a mashed-through notice never leaves a player who switched protection on unprotected; only display mode and master volume are debounced (`SETTINGS_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]`, Tuning Knobs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* and it is flushed on page close, on Save & Quit and on exit. A write failure keeps the values in memory and retries at the next flush; **when the store cannot be written the layer shows one plain ship-log line once per process** (the first failed write, `ct.*` key, placeholder copy "Settings could not be saved."), never again in that process, so a read-only store does not nag on every launch. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: placement, lifetime and fit.)* **Surface:** the line is one `LABEL_1` reading-face line in the **reserved settings-line slot** of the surface that is showing when the failure is detected: on S9 (the notice) under the dismiss item; on S6 (Display & Comfort) between the last control and the Back hint (the slot is always present and empty otherwise, so it never reflows the page, CT-17's invariant; D.1c and D.1d include it in the fit math at the spatial rows). If the failure is detected while neither surface is showing (a debounced flush on page close, on Save & Quit or on exit), the line is armed and drawn in the slot of the next S6 or S9 that opens, or in the panel's status-line slot (CT-17) if the panel is showing and `FAILED` is not, and is never drawn at exit. **Lifetime:** it stays until that surface closes, is then consumed and never returns in the process. At the compact rows (`m < 1`, DEFERRED-REACHABLE) the S6 slot is not reserved and the line is logged only (OQ-CT-40). A capture is owed (AC-CT-136). The few-hundred-byte write is on the UI thread and no thread is introduced. **First-launch default of reduce flashing is ON** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the creative-director's recommendation (the safe direction: a crash or a mashed-through notice otherwise leaves the player who needed protection unprotected) is adopted (OQ-CT-7, D79; the Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline amends its PR-13 hook default to match). The ruling covers reduce flashing only; reduced motion keeps the pipeline's hook default. A fresh store therefore reads `reduce_flashing = true`, and the effective re-open interval at first launch is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` (CT-3). The Chart Table registers zero blocks, hooks, commands and mutators (CT-27).
392	*Source.* KRN CR-16; PCI:845; PIPE:301. **-> ADR candidate (c):** the store mechanism (a `ConfigFile` at `user://settings.cfg` is the working proposal; NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference) and its Alpha replacement.

394	**CT-20. First-launch photosensitivity notice.**

401	*Rule.* One action calls Save/Load's `save_and_quit()`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the call's blocking behaviour is stated.)* **Call contract (this layer's requirement of Save/Load, ASK-CT-7):** the layer disables every item and **presents one frame** before it makes the call, so the disabled styling is on screen before any work; the call must return promptly with `REFUSED_DOWNED` (the same fact as `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`) or `STARTED`, and report completion through a signal or the published `save_status` (`WRITTEN`, `FAILED`) rather than by blocking the frame loop for the write, because a blocked loop freezes the panel and invites an Alt-F4 mid-write. Save/Load's timeout `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is Save/Load's value, default 3 000 ms (range 2 000-15 000) since 2026-10-28; the time to a visible `FAILED` is that timeout, which is within this layer's 3 000 ms ceiling (nothing visible is allowed during the wait, SL-24, and a longer frozen-looking panel invites an Alt-F4 mid-write; ASK-CT-18 answered; Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2, creative-director lean, horror-tone reasons). This layer holds no timer of its own: it never times the write, it reacts only to Save/Load's published facts (`save_status`, `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`); `save_status` is sticky across earlier autosave failures, so `quit_held`, not a stale `FAILED`, is the trigger for a held quit. On `quit_write_active` rising while not already in `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` the layer locks as TX-39. On `quit_held` rising the layer shows `SAVE_FAILED` as TX-23. When the player returns to play (Resume, `chart_table` close, Back to `CLOSED`) while `quit_held` is true or after a `UI3_PLATE` raised by `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, the layer calls Save/Load's `cancel_held_close()` once (idempotent); it does not call it when the exit ends in the Quit-without-saving hold *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*. AC-CT-137 and AC-CT-139 are the checks. **Save/Load's `save_and_quit` itself calls `request_shutdown` after `WRITTEN`, or after an unchanged-state-hash skip that writes nothing (SL-6); the layer calls nothing on that path and never waits on `WRITTEN` as an exit guard.** The item is enabled iff `PauseGate.can_save_quit` (CT-4); otherwise it is disabled (the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7). While the write runs (state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`, this GDD's own label and not a Save/Load name) all items are disabled, `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored, and **nothing is added to the screen**: no spinner, no ring, no bar, no percentage, no toast, no text change (SL UI-2; SL H5; SL-24). If any bound seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD` (the `DEAD` case is unreachable in the solo MVP, SL-6), nothing is written and the result `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` opens **`UI3_PLATE`**, the UI-3 message plate: a string stating that the newest autosave will be used (Continue restores the newest verified generation), **Back** (default focus, non-destructive) and **Quit without saving** (the destructive item, under hold-to-confirm, CT-22). A held or failed write (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, Save/Load's) lands in **`SAVE_FAILED`, which is the panel itself** with the plain word `FAILED` (a word, never colour, never Alarm Red: a save is not an instrument, HR-4) in the panel's status-line position (CT-17): the four items stay in CT-3 order, and Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort and `chart_table` all work (SL:785: "the pause panel stays"). Accepting Save & Quit there opens `UI3_PLATE` with **Retry** (default focus, non-destructive; to `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`) and **Quit without saving** (hold). Completing the UI-3 hold calls `request_shutdown` once (CR-15) with no write; further input is ignored. `save_status` is a sticky read the layer never clears. `UI3_PLATE` is a full-bleed **message plate** (CT-28) in place of the panel *(orchestrator ruling: UI-3's string is a paragraph and the panel is too narrow for the 45-75 character reading measure at 4 of 6 canvases, ui-programmer finding X1 option (a); OQ-CT-12)*. No death language anywhere (SL:993 list).
